statement: Response prevention raises the agent's own predicted risk during treatment: the short-term cost of the intervention is real, and the model produces it without any fear-extinction machinery
metric: mean P(hazard at commitment) during tx: erp_k0 vs free_choice

statement: Response prevention is NOT a probe of one's own efficacy: with no compulsive history to contrast against, k=0 moves the p-marginal by exactly nothing, however long it is applied
metric: |E[p] at end of treatment - prior E[p]|: erp_naive vs erp_k0

statement: ERP after a compulsive block works INDIRECTLY: the earlier fixed-k data fixes the composite lambda_k, k=0 fixes q, and the two together determine p. ERP is the second half of a contrast
metric: entropy of p removed during tx: erp_naive vs erp_k0

statement: What restores knowledge is the CONTRAST between distinct values of k. Locking k at its pre-treatment value -- identical action count, zero diversity -- leaves the agent stuck
metric: gain in log posterior density at the truth: best diversified condition vs locked_k

statement: Confidence is not knowledge: the untreated agent ends up confidently wrong, its posterior placing the true baseline hazard many posterior standard deviations away
metric: posterior z-score of the true q at follow-up: free_choice vs variable_k

statement: Reassurance does what it is for: it removes STATE uncertainty ('am I safe right now?') at the moment of commitment
metric: state entropy removed by the check during tx: reassurance vs free_choice

statement: Reassurance leaves STRUCTURAL knowledge essentially where it found it, unlike diversified exposure
metric: gain in log posterior density at the truth: reassurance vs variable_k

statement: Checking BEFORE acting is diagnostic where checking AFTER acting is not: the same behaviour, moved to a different epistemic position, becomes informative
metric: gain in log posterior density at the truth: baseline_check vs reassurance

statement: Knowledge acquired during treatment persists into free-choice follow-up

The trap does not only produce too much safety behaviour. The untreated agent settles into a badly underestimated baseline hazard and therefore acts LESS than the truth warrants; every condition that corrects q ends up acting more
metric: mean k at follow-up: best diversified condition vs free_choice

statement: The untreated agent is not merely uncertain about the baseline hazard, it is confidently wrong about it
metric: posterior z-score of the true q at follow-up: free_choice vs variable_k
